name: Lightspeed Loyalty
oneLiner: Loyalty add-on for Lightspeed Restaurant POS. The points-based Lightspeed Loyalty (L-Series) adds rewards with email, SMS and push campaigns; a newer card-linked Lightspeed Loyalty, released in Australia in February 2026, tallies spend from repeat card payments inside Lightspeed POS and Payments.
bestFor: Restaurants, cafes and bars already on Lightspeed Restaurant that want loyalty from their POS vendor without a separate loyalty provider.

customers.name: Miriam / 6R Hospitality Group (New York) - Lightspeed Restaurant customer

updates.text: Launched Lightspeed AI, conversational assistants inside Lightspeed Restaurant (and Retail), with more features promised through 2026.
Q3 product release added Tempo (service pacing from kitchen display data) and Tasks (digital opening and closing checklists) to Lightspeed Restaurant.

Released a card-linked Lightspeed Loyalty that tallies eligible spend from repeat card payments, so guests need no loyalty card or app; staff are prompted to enroll guests and apply rewards, and it works across a company's locations. Available in Australia for sites using Lightspeed Payments.

features: Points earned on purchases, redeemed at the POS or online
Birthday campaign with a yearly one-time reward
Time Away campaign giving bonus points to guests who haven't visited in 30 days
Customer segments by spend and visit frequency
Email and SMS campaigns with a drag-and-drop builder (Advanced Marketing)
Automated flows for first purchase, birthdays and lapsed guests
Tiered programs with higher earn rates for VIP groups
Loyalty app / web sign-up for guests
White-labeled points-based rewards, with a Loyalty manager to add and remove points and credit (L-Series)
Promotional SMS, email and push notifications, and campaigns to create VIPs and recapture inactive customers (L-Series)

Card-linked version (Australia): spend tracked through a tokenized card ID, POS prompts to enroll guests by name and mobile number, QR sign-up, Apple and Google Wallet passes, Kiosk and customer display
Free one-on-one onboarding and 24/7 support (per the UK loyalty page)

pricing.text: Sold as an add-on to a Lightspeed Restaurant subscription; price varies by country. Lightspeed's Australian pricing page lists Lightspeed Loyalty from $39/month (AUD); the UK loyalty pricing page's description says prices start at £49 a month. The US site lists no loyalty price: its loyalty pages redirect to the Lightspeed Restaurant pages, whose POS plans are Starter 69 USD, Essential 189 USD and Premium 399 USD.

notes: lightspeedhq.com could not be fetched; facts come from search snippets of Lightspeed pages and release notes. Dropped from the original: 'loyalty included in all plans' (sources conflict; the UK page says loyalty can be bought as an add-on), the $69 Starter plan (third-party sources say it was dropped), the retail Core $149 plan, and the Toast $185/month comparison. Merchant Maverick reports the original L-Series Loyalty is no longer sold to new customers, who get Advanced Loyalty and Marketing (powered by Marsello) instead; I couldn't confirm this on a Lightspeed page. The three customers are Lightspeed Restaurant POS customers; their stories don't confirm they use the loyalty module, so the review calls them Lightspeed Restaurant customers. 2026-11 update: lightspeedhq.com pages fetched directly with curl. The US loyalty page (/pos/restaurant/loyalty/) now redirects to /pos/restaurant/ and the US loyalty pricing page redirects to the POS pricing page, which lists Starter 69, Essential 189 and Premium 399 USD with no loyalty line, so the earlier '$189/$399 loyalty' reading was dropped from the review. UK loyalty page: 'Compatible with Restaurant (L Series) only', add-on to an existing Lightspeed subscription, free onboarding, unlimited 24/7 support. UK loyalty pricing page body is empty; its meta description says 'Prices starting at £49 a month'. AU O-Series pricing lists 'Lightspeed Loyalty From $39/month' (AUD site). G2 has Lightspeed Restaurant (POS) at 4.3 from 55 reviews but no Lightspeed Loyalty listing, so no rating is given.
pros: Points and rewards run in the same POS that takes orders and payments, so staff don't switch systems
One vendor and one support team for POS and loyalty, with free onboarding and 24/7 support (UK page)
Points-based version adds segments, email, SMS and push campaigns, and automated flows for birthdays and lapsed guests
Card-linked version (Australia, 2026) needs no app or loyalty card, and rewards work across locations

cons.text: Works only with Lightspeed Restaurant; the UK page says the points-based Lightspeed Loyalty is compatible with Restaurant (L-Series) only
The card-linked version is available only in Australia, for sites using Lightspeed Payments
The card-linked version is deliberately simple: earn and redeem without campaigns, segments or marketing tools
No published US loyalty price; the US loyalty pages redirect to the main Lightspeed Restaurant pages

plans.billing: monthly add-on to a Lightspeed Restaurant subscription; varies by country
